sumInsured: As per Policy Schedule (examples shown: ₹2L/₹3L/₹4L/₹5L/₹7L/₹10L; illustrations also show ₹3,00,000)

great.name: Automatic Recharge
great.quote: “The Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the Sum Insured once in a policy year... The Recharge shall be utilized only after the Sum Insured and No Claims Bonus (Benefit – 7) has been completely exhausted in that Policy Year”
great.explanation: Automatically reinstates up to 100% of the Sum Insured once in a policy year after your base Sum Insured and accumulated No Claims Bonus are fully exhausted. This gives you an extra layer of coverage for later claims in the same year.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.”
good.reference: Exclusions > Standard Exclusions > Wait Period > Pre-Existing Diseases (Clause 4.1(a)(i)(a))
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date with the insurer. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from the policy start date, while accidents are covered during this period. This is the usual market structure for new policies.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...”
good.reference: Exclusions > Standard Exclusions > Specific Waiting Period (Clause 4.1(a)(ii)(a))
good.explanation: Listed diseases/procedures are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a common specific-illness waiting period.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: “The Recharge shall be available only for all future Claims which are not in relation to any Illness or Injury for which a Claim has already been admitted for that Insured Person during that Policy Year.”
good.explanation: Recharge can be used only for future claims that are not related to the same illness/injury for which a claim was already admitted in that policy year. This limits refill usefulness for repeat admissions of the same condition within the year.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “Under Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 30 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital”
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 30 days immediately before hospital admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “Under Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 60 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the Hospital.”
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 60 days immediately after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines after hospitalization.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “The Company will indemnify the Insured Person... up to the Sum Insured... for the Medical Expenses incurred towards Domiciliary Hospitalization”
good.explanation: Pays for eligible medical expenses for domiciliary hospitalization (treatment at home) up to the Sum Insured, subject to policy conditions. This can help when hospitalization is not possible and home care is medically required.

good.name: No Claims Bonus
good.quote: “enhance the Sum Insured by 10% flat, on a cumulative basis... (i) ... shall not exceed 50%... (ix) In the event of a Claim... accrued No Claims Bonus will be reduced by 10% of the Sum Insured...”
good.explanation: Sum Insured increases by 10% per claim-free year up to a maximum of 50%. If you make a claim, the accumulated bonus reduces by 10% (instead of resetting to zero), which preserves part of your increased cover.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “If the Policy Schedule states 'up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day' as eligible Room Rent, it means the maximum eligible Room Rent... is limited to 1% of the Sum Insured per day of Hospitalization.”
bad.reference: Benefit 1 > Conditions applicable > Room Rent/Room Category (Clause 3.1.1(iii)(a), point 2)
bad.explanation: Room rent can be capped at 1% of the Sum Insured per day if stated in the Policy Schedule. A room-rent cap can increase out-of-pocket costs and may also trigger proportionate deductions on other hospital bills.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: “If the Insured Person is admitted... where the Room Category opted or Room Rent incurred is higher than the eligible... then, The Insured Person shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses...”
bad.reference: Benefit 1 > Conditions applicable > Room Rent/Room Category (Clause 3.1.1(iii)(a))
bad.explanation: If you choose a room category or room rent higher than what is eligible, you must bear a ratable proportion of the associated medical expenses. This can sharply reduce claim payout beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: “The Company will indemnify... for Expenses incurred in respect of the below mentioned Ailments / Procedures up to the amount specified against each and every Ailment / Procedure mentioned in the Policy Schedule...”
bad.reference: Benefit 1 > Expenses incurred on treatment for Named Ailments / Procedures (Clause 3.1.1(iii)(C))
bad.explanation: Named ailments/procedures are payable only up to the amount specified in the Policy Schedule. Even with a high Sum Insured, these sub-limits can cap what you actually get for those treatments.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – II to Policy Terms & Conditions).”
bad.reference: Specific Exclusions > Permanent Exclusions (Clause 4.2(a)(1)) + Annexure II
bad.explanation: Items listed as non-medical in Annexure II (consumables) are not payable. This can add meaningful out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “The Co-payment proportion as specified in the Policy Schedule, shall be borne by the Policyholder / Insured Person on each Claim...”
bad.reference: General Conditions Applicable To All Benefits (Clause 3.A(2))
bad.explanation: A co-payment applies on each claim as per the percentage mentioned in the Policy Schedule. This means you will pay part of every admissible claim from your pocket, which is a major cost risk.

bad.name: Domiciliary Exclusions
bad.quote: “Any Medical Expenses incurred for the treatment in relation to any of the following diseases shall not be payable under this Benefit: 1. Asthma; 2. Bronchitis; ... 5. Diabetes Mellitus... 7. Hypertension; 8. Influenza, cough or cold; ... 12. Arthritis, Gout and Rheumatism.”
bad.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization does not pay for home treatment related to several common conditions like asthma, diabetes, hypertension, influenza/cold, and arthritis. This significantly reduces the practical usefulness of the home-treatment benefit.

unclear.name: ICU Charges
unclear.quote: “The Policy Schedule will specify the limit of ICU Charges applicable... If the Policy Schedule states 'up to 2% of the Sum Insured per day'... ... If the Policy Schedule states... 'no sub-limit'...”
unclear.explanation: ICU charges may be either capped (e.g., 2% of Sum Insured per day) or have no sub-limit depending on what your Policy Schedule states. Your out-of-pocket cost in ICU can vary significantly based on which limit applies to your plan variant.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
